A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CreatiLayout work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplements support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation and layout-planning experiments, ablations, efficiency comparisons, and a supplementary user study.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation, layout-planning, ablation, and efficiency results in Tables 2–7 and the accompanying figures.

M1.justification: SiamLayout's attention branches, training losses, timestep sampling, inference procedure, and LayoutDesigner remain unchanged. The FLUX and LoRA adaptations were already documented in v2 Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions retain LayoutSAM/LayoutSAM-Eval, COCO 2017, T2I-CompBench, and the same three layout-planning tasks. The removed user study changes how generated images are evaluated, without establishing different data or generation-task coverage.

E2.justification: Removing v2 Appendix D/Figure 11 eliminates the human comparison against GLIGEN, MIGC, InstanceDiff, and HiCo. Comparator membership remains unchanged in all retained tables and qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 removes the user-study protocol involving 100 randomly sampled examples and win rates across nine quality criteria. Retained experiments preserve their splits, metrics, training settings, and three-shot layout-planning evaluation.

E4.justification: The architecture and training-strategy ablations, LoRA/compute comparison, and modality-competition analysis retain the same evidence. The removed user study was a separate quality comparison rather than an ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The removed user-study win rates were point estimates without accompanying uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 removes the user-study findings, including SiamLayout-SD3's 87% text and 85% aesthetic win rates in v2 Figure 11. Numerical entries in Tables 2–7 and all retained graphical and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, attention formulations, and training objectives in Equations 1–12 are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or removed.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly describes SiamLayout, LayoutSAM, and LayoutDesigner together as CreatiLayout, but these components and their combined capabilities were already presented in v2. The principal contribution and performance claims retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the concern about detector-induced annotation noise and its unknown performance impact with calls to improve control for many-entity layouts and text-rich entities. The LLM computation limitation and end-to-end future direction remain.

D1.justification: v3's abstract explicitly identifies the existing project link as an access point for code, model, and dataset; v2 merely displays the link. Implementation, hardware, training, annotation, and LoRA details remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish a new resource release.

R1.justification: v3 adds seven references, including MagicMotion, dense-blob generation, UniGen, and several video-diffusion works. These mainly expand citation lists in Section 2; the central positioning around MM-DiT layout control remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose reductions, clarifies the CreatiLayout umbrella name, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence remains intact; appendix lettering changes after the user-study removal.

P2.justification: Several central displays undergo substantial resizing and redistribution: Table 2 and the benchmark and planner qualitative comparisons shrink from full-width to single-column displays. The annotation pipeline moves from v2 supplementary Figure 12 to v3 main Figure 4, and the user-study chart disappears. Retained figure content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the system framing and identifies dense-layout/text challenges, but removes the only human evaluation, including evidence about text and portrait quality, without replacement. It also drops the annotation-noise caveat and reduces the legibility of key comparisons through shrinking. The unchanged methods and benchmark results preserve the main contribution, but these losses outweigh the limited editorial gains.
